This one is, well, interesting. To be honest I'm not really sure what to crosslink it with. I did see that there is a nod to the O5 Council there, and it is a simple matter to turn that into a link to the O5 Dossier. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

Due to recent incidents, experimentation of SCP-829 on animals requires Level 4 authorization. Experimentation on any member of the following taxonomic orders requires O5 authorization: Carnivora, Chiroptera, Crocodilia, Falconiformes, Piciformes, Primates (excepting humans), Proboscidea, Strigiformes, and Struthioniformes.

To this:

Due to recent incidents, experimentation of SCP-829 on animals requires Level 4 authorization. Experimentation on any member of the following taxonomic orders requires O5 authorization: Carnivora, Chiroptera, Crocodilia, Falconiformes, Piciformes, Primates (excepting humans), Proboscidea, Strigiformes, and Struthioniformes.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm afraid I have to downvote this one. The use of pronouns outside of 'it' usually get an immediate downvote from me if the rest of content can't make up for it, which this article didn't. It's just sort of a 'this is a thing that does a thing', which I loath in many series I articles.

But what really sealed the downvote was this line:

Dr. ████████ was brought in to assist researching Subject 829-14, a 28-year-old Asian-American female.

I see no reason to include the race of the individual other than for perverted reasons, which sealed my downvote. I'm sorry, but, I just can't. But maybe I'm seeing things where nothing was really intended, I don't know, but I just can't shake the vibe that it was the intention.

If someone can tell me this, please, let me know.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Although the basic concept is interesting, mind-controlling nail polish? Come on, man… I do not think I can suspend my disbelief enough for me to like this SCP.

On a different note, I found specifying when cutting with 829-treated nails ceases to be effective as "metal and concrete harder than bronze" highly at odds with the Foundation's scientific approach to its project. On one hand, what about materials harder than bronze which are neither metal nor concrete/stone? On the other, referring to bronze instead quoting concrete numbers is hardly precise - especially given bronze is an alloy and as such its hardness can greatly vary. Anyway, I've just replaced that bit with a reference to a real-life material-hardness test and given a concrete value of 120 (FYI, according to Wikipedia, Vickers hardness of bronze is 60-258). Hope you too shall find it better this way!

I would love to somehow put back in some of the original details of the evisceration, but at this point I don't think I could without making it sound like smut (again). item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I think the horror of the killing method needs to be amped up somehow, but there are other things that might spice the article up a bit:

-Perhaps subjects become violent when you try to take away SCP-829, using their sharpened fingernails to slice up anyone that gets in their way, and feeds their blood to 829 once they get it back. Subjects in this "rage state" appear unaware of pain, but can still be killed normally, since that and their sharp fingernails are their only enhancements.

-Outside the "rage state", subjects seem perfectly lucid and rational, and will deny being influenced by 829. They are also no more reckless in their choice of victims than their personality would dictate, and take every precaution to avoid attracting unwanted attention or being caught by law enforcement. Basically, anybody fully under 829's influence becomes a serial killer, but is no more successful at it than they would have been without 829 aside from its assistance in luring and controlling victims. Maybe 829 came to Foundation attention through a high-profile series of murders that turned out to have been committed by an 829 "cult"?

-Possibly up the amount of influence exerted by the touch of 829-painted nails. A researcher was interviewing a test subject, who attempted to seduce him/her and brushed him/her with a nail. Later (hours or days), said researcher tried to get 829 to the test subject, possibly leading to a containment breach.

-Make 829 addictive, with nasty withdrawal symptoms. Test subjects deprived of access to 829 become agitated, and eventually begin bleeding themselves (starting in unobtrusive locations) and painting their nails in their own blood. This behavior escalates with extended deprivation, eventually leading (in the absence of intervention) to death by exsanguination.

  • When SCP-829 has received enough blood, the subject can make her fingernails sharp enough to shred fabrics and easily slice through flesh, while having little effect on metals or stones harder than bronze.
